body:
The twenty-sixth of September keeps books. It inventories a visit. It cancels a calendar. It lets a mass be said where heads once fell.

I. Eight lines from Beijing

On Saturday Beijing publishes the ledger Washington would not read aloud on Friday. Eight points. No poetry.

Strategic stability. APEC in Shenzhen, the G20 in Miami. Tehran is to build no bomb. No transit fees on international waterways — a sentence that means Hormuz and will not say the name. A trade council. Tariff cuts on some thirty billion dollars. An AI channel. A military crisis memorandum. Two pandas for Atlanta. Ten million tonnes of American coal. Xi is back in Beijing. Taiwan stays unsolved. The visit has changed rooms. It has not thickened the treaty.

The thrones still talk about the tap. They do not turn it.

II. Seven days, one refusal

Araghchi sent the plan through Qatar. Lift the blockade. Waive the oil sanctions. Release frozen funds. Hormuz on the sixth day. Nuclear talks on the seventh.

On the White House lawn, before Tennessee, Trump says he rejects their proposal. He will talk. Not on these terms. Thirteen ships pass. The tanker Seaways Sabine runs dark.

III. Twenty minutes in New York

Wadephul sits with Lavrov. Grain across the Black Sea. Leipzig named. Lavrov says the telephone would have done. A handshake. The lights stay on. So does the cold.

Moscow will see the war through to the end. Trump tells Zelenskyy to come to terms with Putin. No line on the ground moves.

IV. In daylight over Kyiv

Seven dead in Kyiv. Among them a fourteen-year-old boy. Klitschko counts forty-six injured. A licence is paper. Paper does not catch a ballistic missile.

V. The square that fills

Leo XIV says mass at the Concorde. Seven to eight hundred thousand. Macron is absent. Marine Le Pen is there. Then Lourdes.

VI. At the edge of the page

Dera Ismail Khan: twelve dead. Bangkok names the flood a disaster. A nor’easter cancels four hundred flights. The Triumf burns off Kamchatka. Seventeen die in a tavern in Carletonville.

The chronicler’s close

Eight points without the files that cut. A refusal of seven days. A handshake without grain. A square full of flags. No thread ends today.

The World Book does not close. It leaves a finger in the pages and waits for 27 September.
